gymExerciseProgress.emptyMessage: Log this exercise 3+ times to see progress

press: Set your feet, grip just outside shoulder width and brace your core.
Lower under control until the bar or handles reach chest level, elbows at about 45°.
Press back up and stop just short of locking out, keeping shoulders down.
squat: Bar high on the back, feet shoulder width, toes turned out slightly.
Sit down between your hips until thighs pass parallel, knees tracking over toes.
Drive through mid-foot and stand tall without letting the chest drop.
hinge: Hips back, chest proud, bar close to the shins with a neutral spine.
Push the hips back until you feel the hamstrings load, bar grazing the legs.
Squeeze the glutes to stand up — the bar path stays vertical.
row: Set a stable torso angle and pull the shoulder blades down first.
Row to the lower ribs, elbows past the body, no shrugging.
Lower under control for a full stretch before the next rep.
curl: Elbows pinned to the ribs, wrists neutral, shoulders relaxed.
Curl until the forearm passes vertical without swinging the torso.
Lower slowly for three counts — the negative is the work.
raise: Slight forward lean, elbows soft, weights beside the thighs.
Lift out to shoulder height leading with the elbows, not the hands.
Pause a beat at the top, then lower under tension.
push: Stand a step back from the stack, elbows tight to your sides.
Extend to full lockout, pausing briefly with the triceps contracted.
Return only until the forearms reach parallel to keep tension.
cardio: Warm up for three to five minutes at an easy pace.
Hold each interval at its target speed — breathing hard but able to speak a word.
Finish with two minutes of walking to bring the heart rate down.
other: Set up so the working muscle is the only thing moving.
Move through the full range you can control, no bouncing.
Match last session’s numbers before adding weight.

aiConsent.title: AI features and usage data
aiConsent.body:
Meal photos and a summary of your logged data are processed by Google Gemini so scanning, insights and Ask Lume can work. Google processes them only to provide those features. Anthropic would receive the summary instead only if we switch on our backup AI provider.

Lume also counts which features you use — never what you log, never your food, weights or notes, and never sold.

You can turn either off any time in Settings → Privacy.

healthDisclaimer.text: Lume provides general nutrition and fitness information. It is not medical advice. Consult a healthcare professional before making significant changes to your diet or exercise routine.

healthDisclaimer.notMedicalAdvice: Lume provides general nutrition and fitness information.
healthDisclaimer.notMedicalDevice: It is not medical advice, it is not a medical device, and it does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent any condition.
healthDisclaimer.consultProfessional: Always consult a qualified healthcare professional before making decisions about your diet, exercise, medication or health — particularly if you are pregnant or nursing, are under 18, or have a medical condition or a history of disordered eating.
healthDisclaimer.neverDisregard: Never disregard professional medical advice, or delay seeking it, because of something you read in the app.
healthDisclaimer.emergency: If you think you may have a medical emergency, contact your doctor or your local emergency service immediately.
healthDisclaimer.targetsFormulas: Calorie and macro targets are calculated from standard published formulas using the information you provide.
healthDisclaimer.targetsStartingPoint: They are a starting point, not a prescription.
healthDisclaimer.ownRisk: You rely on the app’s estimates and insights at your own risk.
